headline: 4 held for using proxy candidates in govt job recruitment
summary: The fraud was uncovered when the candidates' faces did not match the photos on their admit cards during joining day at the Secretariat.
details: Four men were detained after attempting to join as office assistants at the Ministry of Public Administration. The fraud was discovered when their faces did not match the photos on their viva voce (oral exam) admit cards.
The detained individuals are Md. A. Alim from Tangail, Md. Ali Haidar from Sirajganj, Md. Russell Rana Liton from Kurigram, and Md. Masud Fakir from Gazipur.
Upon questioning, the four men admitted that they did not take the oral exams themselves, but instead hired proxy candidates to appear on their behalf.
The Ministry of Public Administration has filed a complaint with the Shahbagh Police Station regarding the incident.
According to the reports, the oral exams took place between June 24 and June 28. The ministry had previously selected 20 people for the office assistant positions.
The fraud was caught on July 19, when the candidates were asked to report to the Joint Secretary (Administration) at the Secretariat's Building 1, Room 1802, to submit their joining letters.
The recruitment process began in May with over 23,000 applicants for the office assistant role, from which 107 were shortlisted for the oral exams.
caption:
They passed the exam, but their faces didn't match. 4 men were caught using proxies to cheat their way into government jobs.

Four men were detained after attempting to join as office assistants at the Ministry of Public Administration. The fraud was discovered when their faces did not match the photos on their viva voce (oral exam) admit cards.

The detained individuals are Md. A. Alim from Tangail, Md. Ali Haidar from Sirajganj, Md. Russell Rana Liton from Kurigram, and Md. Masud Fakir from Gazipur.

Upon questioning, the four men admitted that they did not take the oral exams themselves, but instead hired proxy candidates to appear on their behalf.

The Ministry of Public Administration has filed a complaint with the Shahbagh Police Station regarding the incident.

According to the reports, the oral exams took place between June 24 and June 28. The ministry had previously selected 20 people for the office assistant positions.

The fraud was caught on July 19, when the candidates were asked to report to the Joint Secretary (Administration) at the Secretariat's Building 1, Room 1802, to submit their joining letters.

The recruitment process began in May with over 23,000 applicants for the office assistant role, from which 107 were shortlisted for the oral exams.

headline_marked: Trump's visit sparks [[unprecedented security at World Cup final]]
headline: Trump's visit sparks unprecedented security at World Cup final
summary: Fans faced hours of delays at New York-New Jersey Stadium as US Secret Service and TSA airport-style scanners were deployed for the US President's attendance.
details: The 2026 FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina at the New York-New Jersey Stadium was marked by unprecedented security measures due to the presence of US President Donald Trump.
The US Secret Service took charge of stadium security, with the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) providing airport-style scanners and rigorous screening processes for all attendees.

Fans and media personnel reported waiting in lines for up to two hours to enter the stadium, with some being redirected to different gates due to specific security requirements, including the use of security dogs.
Stadium volunteers noted that a significantly higher number of spectators arrived early compared to the previous seven matches of the tournament.
Gates opened at 11:00 AM local time, four hours before the 3:00 PM kickoff, and additional entry points were opened to manage the crowd.
Despite the long queues and strict security, officials stated that the match began on schedule without any delays or disruptions.
caption:
Airport-style scanners and hours of delays. This is how Trump's presence changed the World Cup final.

The 2026 FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina at the New York-New Jersey Stadium was marked by unprecedented security measures due to the presence of US President Donald Trump.

The US Secret Service took charge of stadium security, with the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) providing airport-style scanners and rigorous screening processes for all attendees.

Fans and media personnel reported waiting in lines for up to two hours to enter the stadium, with some being redirected to different gates due to specific security requirements, including the use of security dogs.

Stadium volunteers noted that a significantly higher number of spectators arrived early compared to the previous seven matches of the tournament.

Gates opened at 11:00 AM local time, four hours before the 3:00 PM kickoff, and additional entry points were opened to manage the crowd.

Despite the long queues and strict security, officials stated that the match began on schedule without any delays or disruptions.
